infrared optical constants and absorptance in bulk n-Si depend nonmonotonically on carrier concentration.
infrared absorption in bulk silicon increases with doping up to a certain concentration and then decreases with further doping, and the maximum absorption is observed in the mid-infrared region.

the theoretical and experimental investigation of the infrared optical properties of bulk-doped n-type silicon.
optical properties of doped silicon in the mid-infrared range of wavelengths.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the infrared absorption in doped silicon increases as the electron concentration is increased, and then decreases as the electron concentration exceeds a critical value, depending on the doping level and wavelength.
the infrared optical constants and absorption in bulk-dopped n-Si are not monotonic functions of electron concentration.
the optical constants of heavily doped n-Si depend strongly on the electron concentration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the absorption of bulk doped silicon increases as the electron concentration is increased up to a certain point, then decreases as the carrier concentration is further increased.

the infrared optical properties of bulk doped silicon depend on the electron concentration in a complicated way and cannot be described by the simple Drude model, which predicts monotonically increasing absorption with increasing electron concentration.
the infrared absorptance is a nonmonotonic function of the carrier concentration in the range of electron concentrations 10(17)-1.3 x10(20)cm(-3).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the absorptance of n-type silicon can be increased by doping.
the absorption of light by electrons is a nonlinear function of electron concentration in bulk silicon.
, for bulk silicon, the infrared optical absorption is maximized at intermediate electron concentrations.
